subject.title: fix: add main agent config protection at validation, startup, and doctor layers

question: Should OpenClaw preserve the current configurable default-agent contract, or intentionally migrate the product to require a literal `main` entry in every configured agent list?
rationale: The patch treats `main` as a security invariant, but current routing and validation deliberately support a different configured default; changing that contract affects existing configurations, startup behavior, sessions, and migration policy.

options.title: Preserve Configurable Defaults
options.body: Reject the literal-`main` requirement and narrow the fix to actionable diagnostics or doctor migration for states that demonstrably break routing.

options.title: Require Literal Main
options.body: Adopt the breaking invariant only with explicit maintainer approval, a doctor migration, aligned docs and CLI behavior, and fresh-install plus upgrade proof.

options.title: Treat Direct Edit as Operator Choice
options.body: Close the linked report as expected trusted-operator behavior and document how default-agent selection works when configuration is edited directly.

recommendation.title: Preserve Configurable Defaults
recommendation.body: Reject the literal-`main` requirement and narrow the fix to actionable diagnostics or doctor migration for states that demonstrably break routing.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history is most directly tied to the configurable default-agent resolution contract affected by this decision.
